details: an HTTP/2 connection gives its flow control window back for a handle_stream body as the handler reads it (and for unread bytes when the stream closes), as Go does, so it holds at most 1 MiB of bodies no handler has read; before, 250 streams could park about 250 MiB. Affected: 0.51.1 and earlier.
changelog: - Security (std/http, native backends): an HTTP/2 connection gives its flow control window back for a handle_stream body as the handler reads it (and for unread bytes when the stream closes), as Go does, so it holds at most 1 MiB of bodies no handler has read; before, 250 streams could park about 250 MiB. Affected: 0.51.1 and earlier.
